key_insight: CEDAR, an evidence-citing and self-auditing LLM pipeline, outperformed trained machine-learning comparators in predicting pediatric diabetes outcomes, with the largest gains on sparsely screened outcomes.
clinical_relevance: The findings suggest potential for chart-grounded risk prediction in pediatric diabetes, but do not establish clinical benefit or readiness for deployment.
method: Analyzed structured records and note-derived social determinants for 2,489 youth with type 2 and 4,018 with type 1 diabetes.
Included continuous glucose monitoring data in the type 1 diabetes cohort.
Used 18 months of follow-up to predict seven outcomes at 24 months in type 2 diabetes and four shared outcomes in type 1 diabetes.
evidence_signal: Pooled AUROC was 0.815 versus 0.656–0.700 for comparators in type 2 diabetes and 0.756 versus 0.603–0.631 in type 1 diabetes; only 4 of 70,246 cited values did not match the chart.
watch_item: The abstract does not report external or prospective validation, leaving generalizability and real-world clinical impact uncertain.
paper_title: Agentic LLM reasoning in pediatric diabetes outcome prediction from multimodal medical records
